# Commerce Operations Foundation

Commerce Operations Foundation is a nonprofit organization. The Commerce Operations Foundation is a common language for modern commerce operations, offering a common language for selling channels to speak with fulfillment channels. Commerce Operations Foundation employs 4 people, founded in 2025. Headquartered in Commerce, United States.

## About

The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling

properties.name: Commerce Operations Foundation
properties.description:
The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling channels transform how orders originate, the industry requires a shared operational language that ensures fulfillment, inventory, and order data can move reliably across every part of the ecosystem.

The Foundation stewards the Order Network eXchange (onX), the first open standard that defines how orders, inventory, products, shipments, and returns flow between selling channels, back office systems, and fulfillment networks. Built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), onX provides the common foundation needed for real-time, AI-ready commerce operations.

Guided by four core principles — Open, Neutral, Interoperable, and Extensible — the Foundation maintains the onX specification, oversees its governance, and brings together the organizations shaping the next generation of commerce infrastructure. Through working groups, a technical steering committee, and publicly available reference implementations, the Foundation enables companies to adopt and influence interoperable standards with confidence.

The Commerce Operations Foundation represents a growing global community of retailers, brands, platforms, 3PLs, logistics providers, and technology vendors who share a vision for a more connected, intelligent, and resilient commerce ecosystem. Membership is open to organizations and practitioners committed to advancing open standards that future-proof the industry.

properties.name: Cogent Equity
properties.description:
Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.

 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction

The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

entity.name: Cresora Commerce
entity.description:
Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

entity.name: Commerce Operations Foundation
entity.description:
The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling channels transform how orders originate, the industry requires a shared operational language that ensures fulfillment, inventory, and order data can move reliably across every part of the ecosystem.

The Foundation stewards the Order Network eXchange (onX), the first open standard that defines how orders, inventory, products, shipments, and returns flow between selling channels, back office systems, and fulfillment networks. Built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), onX provides the common foundation needed for real-time, AI-ready commerce operations.

Guided by four core principles — Open, Neutral, Interoperable, and Extensible — the Foundation maintains the onX specification, oversees its governance, and brings together the organizations shaping the next generation of commerce infrastructure. Through working groups, a technical steering committee, and publicly available reference implementations, the Foundation enables companies to adopt and influence interoperable standards with confidence.

The Commerce Operations Foundation represents a growing global community of retailers, brands, platforms, 3PLs, logistics providers, and technology vendors who share a vision for a more connected, intelligent, and resilient commerce ecosystem. Membership is open to organizations and practitioners committed to advancing open standards that future-proof the industry.

entity.name: JoinB2B
entity.description:
The main mission of JoinB2B is to directly and without any mediator match the relevant companies to each other. 
But, how JoinB2B determines which company fits any other specific company? For that, JoinB2B utilizes belowmentioned methods:

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on their own as well as target locations.
It is not surprising that most companies have their target locations for enlarging their businesses along with their location of their operations. For example, if Company “A” selected its location as Germany, Berlin and its target location as Hungary, Budapest while Company “B” selected its location as Hungary, Budapest and its target location as Germany Berlin, then the unique matching system of JoinB2B introduces these two companies to each other. 

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on their business purpose. 

When registering at JoinB2B, the companies are asked about their registration purpose (B2B purpose). For example, if company “A” selected its B2B purpose as “to find a sub-contractor”, while company ”B” selected its B2B purpose as “to become a sub-contractor”, then the unique matching system of JoinB2B introduces these two companies to each other. The companies are able to see the list of the companies matching their B2B purpose easily at the right side of the website. 

JoinB2B matches the companies depending on products/services that they offer and products/services that they demand.

For example, if company “A” is offering a pen while company “B” announces a tender for purchasing a pen, then the system will automatically introduce these two companies to each other. System matches these two companies because their offers and demands are relevant to each other. 

Join B2B provides messaging services to its users to help them to directly, without any obstacles contact each other.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

# Commerce Operations Foundation

Commerce Operations Foundation is a nonprofit organization. The Commerce Operations Foundation is a common language for modern commerce operations, offering a common language for selling channels to speak with fulfillment channels. ## About

The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling

properties.name: Commerce Operations Foundation
properties.description:
The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling channels transform how orders originate, the industry requires a shared operational language that ensures fulfillment, inventory, and order data can move reliably across every part of the ecosystem.

The Foundation stewards the Order Network eXchange (onX), the first open standard that defines how orders, inventory, products, shipments, and returns flow between selling channels, back office systems, and fulfillment networks. Built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), onX provides the common foundation needed for real-time, AI-ready commerce operations.

Guided by four core principles — Open, Neutral, Interoperable, and Extensible — the Foundation maintains the onX specification, oversees its governance, and brings together the organizations shaping the next generation of commerce infrastructure. Through working groups, a technical steering committee, and publicly available reference implementations, the Foundation enables companies to adopt and influence interoperable standards with confidence.

The Commerce Operations Foundation represents a growing global community of retailers, brands, platforms, 3PLs, logistics providers, and technology vendors who share a vision for a more connected, intelligent, and resilient commerce ecosystem. Membership is open to organizations and practitioners committed to advancing open standards that future-proof the industry.

Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

entity.name: Commerce Operations Foundation
entity.description:
The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling channels transform how orders originate, the industry requires a shared operational language that ensures fulfillment, inventory, and order data can move reliably across every part of the ecosystem.

The Foundation stewards the Order Network eXchange (onX), the first open standard that defines how orders, inventory, products, shipments, and returns flow between selling channels, back office systems, and fulfillment networks. Built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), onX provides the common foundation needed for real-time, AI-ready commerce operations.

Guided by four core principles — Open, Neutral, Interoperable, and Extensible — the Foundation maintains the onX specification, oversees its governance, and brings together the organizations shaping the next generation of commerce infrastructure. Through working groups, a technical steering committee, and publicly available reference implementations, the Foundation enables companies to adopt and influence interoperable standards with confidence.

The Commerce Operations Foundation represents a growing global community of retailers, brands, platforms, 3PLs, logistics providers, and technology vendors who share a vision for a more connected, intelligent, and resilient commerce ecosystem. Membership is open to organizations and practitioners committed to advancing open standards that future-proof the industry.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

properties.name: Cogent Equity
properties.description:
Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

# Commerce Operations Foundation

Commerce Operations Foundation is a nonprofit organization. The Commerce Operations Foundation is a common language for modern commerce operations, offering a common language for selling channels to speak with fulfillment channels. ## About

The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling

properties.name: Commerce Operations Foundation
properties.description:
The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling channels transform how orders originate, the industry requires a shared operational language that ensures fulfillment, inventory, and order data can move reliably across every part of the ecosystem.

The Foundation stewards the Order Network eXchange (onX), the first open standard that defines how orders, inventory, products, shipments, and returns flow between selling channels, back office systems, and fulfillment networks. Built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), onX provides the common foundation needed for real-time, AI-ready commerce operations.

Guided by four core principles — Open, Neutral, Interoperable, and Extensible — the Foundation maintains the onX specification, oversees its governance, and brings together the organizations shaping the next generation of commerce infrastructure. Through working groups, a technical steering committee, and publicly available reference implementations, the Foundation enables companies to adopt and influence interoperable standards with confidence.

The Commerce Operations Foundation represents a growing global community of retailers, brands, platforms, 3PLs, logistics providers, and technology vendors who share a vision for a more connected, intelligent, and resilient commerce ecosystem. Membership is open to organizations and practitioners committed to advancing open standards that future-proof the industry.

entity.description:
Retailers today need the agility to design and deliver modern store experiences that keep pace with customer expectations. OneView provides a trusted, proven, cloud-native unified commerce platform that replaces legacy in-store software with a unified, composable foundation to power next-generation retail.
Our platform combines digital point of sale, real-time inventory visibility, store fulfillment, enterprise promotions, and clienteling into one cohesive solution. The result is retail agility—faster rollouts, seamless omnichannel engagement and the ability to validate new concepts without disrupting operations.
With OneView, retailers gain:
Control and flexibility to define unique store experiences without software vendor dependency
Stronger margins with process optimization and enterprise-wide transparency
Customer loyalty driven by connected, personalized shopping journeys
Proof of value through rapid deployment and real-world validation


Proven by leading global retailers including Australia Post, Molton Brown, and Forever New, OneView empowers organizations to innovate with confidence, reduce risk, and scale for long-term growth.

The OneView Digital Store Platform combines digital point of sale, real-time inventory management, and enterprise promotions to deliver a comprehensive store solution that drives increased footfalls, expands basket size and maximizes process optimization to improve margins. OneView enables the exchange of powerful store information across the enterprise to positively impact sales, business operations and customer experience. 

Australia Post, Discount Tire Corporation, Molton Brown and Carhartt are among the global retailer leaders revolutionizing their stores with OneView Commerce. 

For more information, visit www.oneviewcommerce.com. Twitter: @oneviewcommerce.

entity.name: Cresora Commerce
entity.description:
Cresora Commerce is an AI-native commerce infrastructure platform built for organizations operating in complex, high-volume, and regulated environments.

Modern commerce has outgrown traditional payment systems. Businesses today manage multiple transaction channels, fragmented financial data, and increasing pressure for speed, accuracy, and auditability. Legacy platforms were not designed for this level of complexity. They process transactions, but they do not orchestrate them.

Cresora solves this by acting as the infrastructure layer that connects systems, orchestrates transaction flow, and reconciles financial activity across the entire commerce lifecycle.

The platform unifies embedded commerce, omnichannel interaction, and financial reconciliation into a single framework. It enables organizations to route transactions across multiple processors, align data across systems, and achieve financial accuracy without manual reconciliation or rigid dependencies.

AI is embedded at the core of Cresora, powering data normalization, transaction matching, anomaly detection, and operational insights. This reduces manual work, accelerates financial close, and improves visibility across operations.

Cresora is processor-agnostic and bank-agnostic, giving organizations the flexibility to scale without being locked into a single provider. Its modular architecture supports enterprises, software platforms, and partner ecosystems that require control, compliance, and precision.

By transforming fragmented systems into a unified infrastructure, Cresora enables organizations to move money more intelligently, operate more efficiently, and achieve financial truth at scale.

entity.name: Cogent Equity
entity.description:
Most transaction risk isn’t created during a sale process - it’s exposed by it.
 
By the time a business goes to market, many of the factors that determine value and deal certainty are already in place. We work with business owners and their advisors to evaluate those factors before the market does.
 
At Cogent Equity, we represent a limited number of companies with $1M to $10M in adjusted EBITDA, typically with long operating histories and strong underlying performance. Our focus is not just on running a process, but on ensuring the business is positioned to succeed in one.
 
This work often begins before a sale is imminent. We evaluate the business the way a sophisticated buyer would - identifying value constraints, aligning expectations, and addressing issues that would otherwise surface during diligence.
 
For advisors, the situations where it tends to be most useful to involve us are:
 
 - An owner is beginning to consider a sale in the next 1–3 years 
 - Valuation expectations are unclear or misaligned 
 - There are known or suspected issues that could impact a transaction 
 
Our perspective is shaped by firsthand experience as owners , operators, buyers, and sellers across nine different industries - allowing me to evaluate businesses the way a sophisticated buyer actually would.
 
While much of our work begins before a sale, we also represent owners through a structured, buyer-focused transaction process when the timing is right.
 
The objective is not just the right deal, but the right buyer - and a process that holds together from start to finish.

La plataforma funciona como el centro de tu operación e-commerce, conectando:
✔️Tu ERP o sistema de gestión (stock, precios y pedidos).

✔️Tus operadores logísticos (transportistas).

entity.name: Commerce Operations Foundation
entity.description:
The Commerce Operations Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit 501(c)(6) industry body dedicated to creating open standards for how modern commerce systems interoperate. As AI, social commerce, and new selling channels transform how orders originate, the industry requires a shared operational language that ensures fulfillment, inventory, and order data can move reliably across every part of the ecosystem.

The Foundation stewards the Order Network eXchange (onX), the first open standard that defines how orders, inventory, products, shipments, and returns flow between selling channels, back office systems, and fulfillment networks. Built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), onX provides the common foundation needed for real-time, AI-ready commerce operations.

Guided by four core principles — Open, Neutral, Interoperable, and Extensible — the Foundation maintains the onX specification, oversees its governance, and brings together the organizations shaping the next generation of commerce infrastructure. Through working groups, a technical steering committee, and publicly available reference implementations, the Foundation enables companies to adopt and influence interoperable standards with confidence.

The Commerce Operations Foundation represents a growing global community of retailers, brands, platforms, 3PLs, logistics providers, and technology vendors who share a vision for a more connected, intelligent, and resilient commerce ecosystem. Membership is open to organizations and practitioners committed to advancing open standards that future-proof the industry.

Go-live in ~18 weeks — not 18 months.

→ Learn more at tenoro.io
